subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Akashi Kaikyo: World's Longest Span
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Akashi Kaikyo: World's Longest Span.

hook.text: Japan's Akashi Kaikyo Bridge spans nearly two kilometers of open water between Kobe and Awaji Island.

buildup.text: Each cable contains 36,830 strands of wire. Laid end to end, the wire would circle the Earth seven times.

discovery.text: During construction, the 1995 Kobe earthquake shifted the towers one meter apart. Engineers redesigned mid-build.

twist.text: Wind tunnel tests used a 40-meter model. The deck has slots that let wind pass through instead of pushing it.

climax.text: The bridge opened in 1998 and handles typhoons and earthquakes. Its design set the standard for long spans.

punchline.text: Nature tried to stop this bridge. Engineering adapted.

quiz.question: What happened to the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge during the 1995 Kobe earthquake?
options: Both main towers collapsed and had to be rebuilt entirely
The towers shifted one meter apart, forcing a redesign
The cables snapped and the deck fell into the strait
